methodology: The decomposition process involved analyzing both the original research topic and the generated technical specification to extract independent and self-contained atomic units. Each unit was evaluated for its technical specificity and unambiguity, ensuring that it could be implemented as a single requirement. The original research topic was broken down into distinct requirements related to the D flip-flops, reset behavior, and clock triggering. The generated specification was similarly dissected to identify the logic functions, interface behaviors, and timing dependencies that correspond to the original requirements.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Each D flip-flop has an active high asynchronous reset.
The output of each D flip-flop is reset to 0 when the reset signal is asserted.
Each D flip-flop samples its D input on the positive edge of the clk signal.
The module is defined as 'module top_module(input clk, input [7:0] d, input areset, output reg [7:0] q);'.
spec_atomic_units: The module 'top_module' implements 8 D flip-flops with an active high asynchronous reset.
The outputs of the flip-flops are reset to 0 when the reset signal is asserted.
Each flip-flop samples its D input on the positive edge of the clk signal.
The module has three input ports: 'clk', 'd', and 'areset'.
The output port 'q' is an 8-bit register.
When 'areset' is high, 'q' is set to 0 immediately.
On the positive edge of 'clk', if 'areset' is low, 'q' is updated to the value of 'd'.
The timing characteristics are defined by the setup and hold times of the D flip-flops.
The non-blocking assignment (<=) is used to update 'q'.
